title: Classes, objects, and encapsulation — Module Quiz
description: Course assessment: A digital wallet protects its balance.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: What does assigning Wallet alias = first copy?

options.text: The balance into a new object

questions.explanation: Both variables can refer to one object.

questions.prompt: Why keep a wallet balance private?

options.text: To enforce valid changes through operations

questions.explanation: Encapsulation protects the invariant through the API.

questions.prompt: Which member belongs to the class rather than each instance?
questions.explanation: Static state is associated with the class.

options.text: A global variable for every field

questions.explanation: Constructor validation prevents invalid instances from escaping.

questions.prompt: If a.equals(b) is true, which must hold?

options.text: a and b have different classes

questions.explanation: The equality contract requires equal hash codes for equal objects.

questions.prompt: Does a private field alone make a class thread-safe?
questions.explanation: Visibility and synchronization are separate concerns.

options.text: A new wallet is allocated, so first is unchanged

questions.explanation: One Wallet object starts with balance 0. first and alias both refer to that same wallet. alias.deposit changes the shared object; first.balance() is 50.
